+//! The wire laws' findings in words (#534 and its children), and the
+//! reading a stated verify tolerance let pass (#1170). Split from the
+//! module head for the 400-line law.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own words over our own laws; no vendor material.
+
+use super::{CutSide, Slug, WireVerdict, SLUG_AREA_TOL};
+use crate::geo2d::Point2;
+
+/// The deepest kerf reading a stated verify tolerance let pass (#1170):
+/// the kerf enters the model's facets by `depth` mm at `at` on the
+/// plane `z`, within the tolerance.
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub struct WireUnder {
+    pub depth: f64,
+    pub z: f64,
+    pub at: Point2,
+}
+
+impl WireUnder {
+    /// The deeper of two readings.
+    pub(super) fn deeper(a: Option<Self>, b: Option<Self>) -> Option<Self> {
+        match (a, b) {
+            (Some(a), Some(b)) => Some(if b.depth > a.depth { b } else { a }),
+            (a, b) => a.or(b),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+/// Every finding refuses: the wire laws have no warning tier.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
+pub enum WireFinding {
+    /// The path cannot be read by these laws (an arc, a posed or
+    /// non-planar move, no moves, a bad offset).
+    Unreadable(String),
+    NoStart,
+    /// The path does not start at the stated start hole.
+    StartMoved { stated: Point2, path: Point2 },
+    /// The product stands nearer the threading point than the kerf.
+    Threading { z: f64, at: Point2, clear: f64, need: f64 },
+    /// An open run's end (where the wire is threaded or cut) stands in
+    /// the stock or nearer it than the kerf.
+    OpenEndInStock { z: f64, at: Point2, clear: f64, need: f64 },
+    /// The kerf of move `move_no` (1-based) enters the product.
+    /// The first move of the first plane that gouges. `tol` is the
+    /// stated verify tolerance the reading is past (0 when none is
+    /// stated) and `deepest` the deepest reading of any move at any
+    /// plane - what a verify tolerance would have to cover (#1170).
+    Gouge { move_no: usize, z: f64, at: Point2, depth: f64, moves: usize, tol: f64, deepest: f64 },
+    /// The closed cut frees no material.
+    NothingFreed { z: f64 },
+    /// The piece freed is not the one the stated side drops.
+    WrongSlug { z: f64, side: CutSide, at: Point2, product_area: f64 },
+    /// The cut frees a piece and nothing holds it: no tabs, no capture
+    /// stated (#290 D6, #539).
+    Unsupported { z: f64, side: CutSide, at: Point2 },
+    /// The main cut of a tabbed path already frees a piece: the tabs do
+    /// not hold it (#539).
+    TabsDoNotHold { z: f64, at: Point2 },
+    /// A burnout (#540) frees a piece: a core is left to drop.
+    Core { z: f64, at: Point2, area: f64 },
+}
+
+impl WireFinding {
+    /// The finding in words, mm.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {
+        match self {
+            WireFinding::Unreadable(why) => format!("the wire laws cannot read the path - {why}"),
+            WireFinding::NoStart => {
+                "no start hole is stated - the wire cannot be threaded, nothing is judged clear".into()
+            }
+            WireFinding::StartMoved { stated, path } => format!(
+                "the path starts at X{:.3} Y{:.3}, not at the stated start hole X{:.3} Y{:.3} - regenerate it",
+                path.x, path.y, stated.x, stated.y
+            ),
+            WireFinding::Threading { z, at, clear, need } => format!(
+                "the start hole at X{:.3} Y{:.3} is not clear for threading at Z{z:.3}: the part stands {} - the wire and its gap need {need:.4} mm all round",
+                at.x,
+                at.y,
+                if *clear <= 0.0 { "at the threading point itself".to_owned() } else { format!("{clear:.4} mm from it") }
+            ),
+            WireFinding::OpenEndInStock { z, at, clear, need } => format!(
+                "the open run's end at X{:.3} Y{:.3} is not clear of the stock at Z{z:.3}: the stock stands {} - the wire is threaded and cut in the air, {need:.4} mm clear all round (regenerate the run against the stock as it stands)",
+                at.x,
+                at.y,
+                if *clear <= 0.0 { "at the point itself".to_owned() } else { format!("{clear:.4} mm from it") }
+            ),
+            WireFinding::Gouge { move_no, z, at, depth, moves, tol, deepest } => format!(
+                "gouge: the kerf of move {move_no} enters the part by {depth:.4} mm near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3}{} ({moves} move(s) gouge{})",
+                at.x,
+                at.y,
+                if *tol > 0.0 { format!(", past the stated verify tolerance {tol:.4} mm") } else { String::new() },
+                if *deepest > *depth + 5e-5 { format!("; the deepest reading at any height is {deepest:.4} mm") } else { String::new() }
+            ),
+            WireFinding::NothingFreed { z } => format!(
+                "the cut frees no material at Z{z:.3} - nothing drops when it closes (no closed cut, or no stock around the opening to judge the slug)"
+            ),
+            WireFinding::WrongSlug { z, side: CutSide::Die, at, product_area } => format!(
+                "slug: the piece freed near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3} holds {product_area:.3} mm² of the part - a die keeps the material outside the cut, but here the part drops",
+                at.x, at.y
+            ),
+            WireFinding::Core { z, at, area } => format!(
+                "core: the burnout frees a piece of {area:.3} mm² near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3} - a burnout must leave no core to drop",
+                at.x, at.y
+            ),
+            WireFinding::WrongSlug { z, side: CutSide::Punch, at, .. } => format!(
+                "slug: the piece freed near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3} holds none of the part - a punch's cut frees the punch, but here only waste drops and the part stays in the skeleton",
+                at.x, at.y
+            ),
+            WireFinding::Unsupported { z, side, at } => format!(
+                "slug: the {} freed near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3} drops unsupported when the cut closes - state tabs to hold it until a tab cut-off, or state that the slug is captured",
+                match side {
+                    CutSide::Die => "slug",
+                    CutSide::Punch => "punch",
+                    CutSide::Open => "piece",
+                },
+                at.x,
+                at.y
+            ),
+            WireFinding::TabsDoNotHold { z, at } => format!(
+                "slug: the main cut already frees the piece near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3} - the tabs do not hold it; place them on the cut that encloses it",
+                at.x, at.y
+            ),
+            WireFinding::WrongSlug { z, side: CutSide::Open, at, .. } => format!(
+                "slug: an open run frees a piece near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{z:.3} - an open run closes no slug",
+                at.x, at.y
+            ),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+
+impl WireFinding {
+    /// The first plane's gouge, its `deepest` raised to a later plane's.
+    pub(super) fn first_gouge(first: Option<Self>, next: Option<Self>) -> Option<Self> {
+        match (first, next) {
+            (Some(WireFinding::Gouge { move_no, z, at, depth, moves, tol, deepest }), Some(WireFinding::Gouge { deepest: more, .. })) => {
+                Some(WireFinding::Gouge { move_no, z, at, depth, moves, tol, deepest: deepest.max(more) })
+            }
+            (first, next) => first.or(next),
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// What a gouge with no verify tolerance stated may be (#1170): the
+    /// caller says it for a cut whose surface the model tessellates.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn facets_hint(&self) -> Option<&'static str> {
+        match self {
+            WireFinding::Gouge { tol, .. } if *tol <= 0.0 => Some(
+                "a tessellated loft's facets stand past its ruled surface by up to the chord tolerance of the model: when the deepest reading is within that, state that tolerance as the cut's verify tolerance",
+            ),
+            _ => None,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl WireVerdict {
+    /// The stated verify tolerance the kerf law judged under, and the
+    /// deepest reading it let pass (#1170); `None` when none is stated.
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn tolerance_said(&self) -> Option<String> {
+        if self.verify_tol <= 0.0 {
+            return None;
+        }
+        Some(match &self.under {
+            Some(u) => format!(
+                "kerf judged under the stated verify tolerance {:.4} mm: the kerf enters the model's facets by at most {:.4} mm, near X{:.3} Y{:.3} at Z{:.3}",
+                self.verify_tol, u.depth, u.at.x, u.at.y, u.z
+            ),
+            None => format!(
+                "kerf judged under the stated verify tolerance {:.4} mm: no reading needed it",
+                self.verify_tol
+            ),
+        })
+    }
+}
+
+/// The pieces a cut frees, in the report line's words.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn slugs_said(s: &[Slug]) -> String {
+    if s.is_empty() {
+        return "frees nothing".into();
+    }
+    s.iter()
+        .map(|g| {
+            format!(
+                "frees {:.2} mm² near X{:.3} Y{:.3} ({})",
+                g.area,
+                g.at.x,
+                g.at.y,
+                if g.product_area > SLUG_AREA_TOL { "the part" } else { "waste" }
+            )
+        })
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        .join(", ")
+}

         taper: false,

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+## #1170 - Wire EDM 4-axis: per-ruling widening and a stated verify tolerance
+
+**Decided:**
+
+*Widening.* A 4-axis cut has a `widening` choice. `PerRuling` is the
+default: each ruling stands off the two profiles by what its own twist
+needs. `Uniform` is the earlier behaviour: every ruling stands off as far
+as the worst one. A project file without the key reads as `PerRuling`,
+and the key is written only for `uniform`. The widening is in the stamp
+digest, because it moves the wire.
+
+The per-ruling path adds a transition ruling 1 mm (`TRANSITION`) in from
+each end of a long span, so a widening ends near the twist and not across
+a whole flank. A transition that changes nothing is pruned, and the path
+is read again after the prune. Each end of a ruling takes its own scale;
+the rulings of a fan take one scale together. After the path is built,
+the existing ruled kerf law judges the emitted wire at every height it
+reads (the whole-law guard). A path that fails it is refused by name; it
+is never emitted.
+
+*Verify tolerance.* A 4-axis cut states `verify_tolerance` (mm, default
+0). The wire verify's kerf law lets a reading enter the model's facets by
+no more than that value. The threading law and the slug law never use it.
+The operation door accepts 0 to 0.25 mm (`VERIFY_TOLERANCE_MAX`). The
+verify refuses, as unreadable, a value that is negative, not finite or
+not below the kerf offset. The value is not in the stamp digest: the
+verify reads it at each post, and the stored path does not depend on it.
+The post gate's report line states the tolerance and the deepest reading
+that it let pass.
+
+*Gouge text.* The kerf law now reads every plane and does not stop at the
+first gouge. The finding keeps the first plane's gouge and adds the
+deepest reading at any height. A 4-axis gouge with no stated tolerance
+adds a hint that names the model's chord tolerance. `slugs_said` moved
+from `app` to `sim`, where the words of the other wire findings are.
+
+*Posted gate.* `posted_gates/wire_4axis.rs` compares its direct
+regeneration with the app's golden by `same_program`: the same lines and
+words, each number within 3 counts (3 um). The two goldens
+(`wire_4axis_punch.cl`, `wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc`) are regenerated;
+their pose words moved by 1 um.
+
+**Why:** A uniform widening makes the straight stretches of a punch
+oversize by the worst twist's amount, which the issue names as the
+defect. The per-ruling result is not unique: several wires hold the kerf
+law, and the one found depends on the vertices of the profile rings. The
+whole-law guard therefore decides safety, not the construction. A
+tessellated loft's facets stand past its ruled surface by up to its chord
+tolerance, so a correct cut reads as a gouge of that size. Only the user
+knows the tolerance the model was made with, so it is a stated parameter
+with a strict default, and the report shows what it excused.
+
+**Considered and dropped:**
+
+- An absent `widening` key that reads as `Uniform`. It keeps old files
+  byte-stable, but the default then differs between a new and an old
+  operation. An old operation's stamp is stale after this change in both
+  cases.
+- One scale for each ruling across its two ends. It widens the flat end
+  of a ruling whose other end twists.
+- No transition rulings. The widening then spreads over the whole length
+  of a flank next to a twist.
+- An enum of the app's own for the widening. The motion type has two
+  plain variants; a copy adds a mapping and no meaning.
+- A verify tolerance for each machine or each document. The chord
+  tolerance belongs to the lofted model of one cut.
+- A tolerance derived from the mesh. The verify cannot know the true
+  surface from the facets alone.
+- A tolerance for the 2-axis and tapered cuts. Their walls are planes or
+  cones over the profile, and the issue asks for the 4-axis cut only.
+- An exact compare in the posted gate. It fails on a 1-3 um difference
+  that comes from the ring representation, not from a defect.
+
+**Cost to change later:** A change of the default widening changes
+posted words of each 4-axis cut and makes each stamp stale. A different
+transition length changes the goldens. Moving the tolerance to a
+different owner needs a project-file migration for `verify_tolerance`.
+
+**Known limits:** The `tangled` refusal of the per-ruling path has no
+fixture that reaches it. The uniform widening folds on the sheared
+fixture with one twisted flank and is refused there; per ruling cuts it.
+The posted program was not run on a real EDM control.

@@ -120,6 +120,25 @@ rulings and an ambiguous whole turn at one endpoint are refused. Separate
 open runs are not stitched into a profile; select a face or one closed
 edge chain.
 
+Where the two profiles turn against each other, a straight wire cannot
+lie in the surface between them: it stands off by up to the twist
+tolerance. **Stand off** says where. **Only where the surface twists**
+(the default) cuts every straight stretch to size and stands the wire
+off at the twist alone. **The same all round** stands every stretch off
+as far as the worst one needs. A twist that needs more than the
+tolerance is refused where it stands.
+
+**Verify tolerance.** The check before posting reads the model's facets.
+A lofted model's facets stand past its true surface by up to the chord
+tolerance the model was faceted at, so a correct 4-axis cut can read as
+a gouge of a few microns. State that tolerance as the cut's **Verify
+tolerance**: the check then lets the kerf into the facets by that much
+and no more, and the report says the deepest reading it let pass. 0 (the
+default) checks the facets as they are. A gouge is always refused with
+the deepest reading at any height, so you can see whether the model's
+tolerance explains it. The value must be below the kerf offset and at
+most 0.25 mm.
+
 **Inside corners.** No inside corner can be cut tighter than the kerf
 offset. A corner, slot or neck the wire cannot reach is refused by name,
 never rounded for you; round it in the model or cut with a thinner wire
